rover.name: Perseverance-class rover (NASA Mars 2020) on the Moon — hypothetical
references: NASA 3D Resources: Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover.glb (github.com/nasa/NASA-3D-Resources); geometry measured in metres, wheel diameter 0.525 m matches the published 52.5 cm
rover.fidelity_warning: Hypothetical: Perseverance is a Mars rover. Its mass, wheels, speed, tilt rating and MMRTG power are NASA-published, and its wheel layout is measured from NASA's to-scale 3D model. It was never qualified for lunar PSR temperatures, and battery capacity is not published, so no shadow-time or battery limit is applied. Mobility and stability results are physically meaningful; endurance is not modelled.

n_wheels.src: six wheels, each with its own motor

grouser_height_m.src: 48 grousers published; height not published (Curiosity-like 7.5 mm assumed)

track_width_m.src: front/rear wheel-centre spacing measured from NASA 3D model

wheelbase_m.src: front-to-rear wheel-centre distance measured from NASA 3D model

wheel_positions_m.src: wheel centres (forward, left) measured from NASA 3D model, relative to wheel centroid

steer_range_deg.src: corner-wheel steering; range not on the NASA page

speed_nominal_mps.src: top speed 152 m/h on flat hard ground (NASA); used as commanded speed

max_slope_req_deg.src: drivers avoid terrain tilting the rover > 30 deg (NASA)

battery_wh.src: two Li-ion batteries; capacity not published

solar_peak_w.src: no solar arrays; MMRTG ~110 W at launch (NASA)

psr_ops_limit_h.src: not qualified for lunar PSR; no limit applied

cg_height_m.src: from the published 45 deg tilt rating: h = half-track(1.062 m) / tan 45

soil.name: Lunar regolith — Apollo LRV design values
soil.src: Costes, Farmer & George (1972) Mobility performance of the Lunar Roving Vehicle; Carrier (1991) Lunar Sourcebook ch. 9; as quoted in Carrier, LGI 'Trafficability of lunar microrovers' Part 1 (docs/references/lgi_trafficability_part1.pdf)

fidelity: Terrain is the LOLA DEM at its native 20 m grid (bilinear). Rocks, boulders and craters smaller than ~20-40 m are invisible to this simulation; VIPER's published 15 cm obstacle limit cannot be checked from this data.
Wheel-soil forces use the Bekker-Wong model with Apollo LRV soil parameters (Costes et al. 1972). Real PSR regolith properties are unmeasured and may differ; see the loose-soil sensitivity run.
Quasi-static model: no dynamics, wheel-level suspension articulation, slip-sinkage or turn-in-place time.
Solar and Earth visibility are long-term AVERAGES (Mazarico et al. 2011), not a time-specific illumination simulation.
Parameters tagged 'assumed' are not published by the agency and are shown in the parameter table.

It was never qualified for lunar PSR temperatures, and battery capacity is not published, so no shadow-time or battery limit is applied. Mobility and stability results are physically meaningful; endurance is not modelled.
